newsitem.title: FRANCE: Socialist govt fails to clarify Eramet position.
newsitem.headline: Socialist govt fails to clarify Eramet position.

text.p: France's new Socialist government said on Wednesday that it would review the situation of mining company Eramet in New Caledonia but failed to clarify its position on this highly-sensitive issue.
In a statement, the office of Prime minister Lionel Jospin said the state's approach would respect the interests of Eramet and of its minority shareholders.
It also said it supported plans to build a new nickel smelter in the north of the overseas territory and ordered a study on its "economic and industrial prospects."
Philippe Essig, a former civil servant and president of state railways operator SNCF, will conduct the study during the summer.
"We think it is positive that the government wants to reconsider the whole issue and consult all players involved," an Eramet spokesman said.

Eramet, the world's third largest nickel producer, and the former conservative government had been caught in a bitter dispute over the distribution of mining rights in the Pacific island of New Caledonia.

The French state, which controls 55 percent of Eramet, wanted to use nickel from one of Eramet's mines to supply a plant that local Kanak company Societe Miniere de Sud Pacifique (SMSP) and Canadian group Falconbridge want to build in the north of the island.
This was aimed at appeasing local separatists ahead of a 1998 referendum on independence for the territory.
But Eramet management opposed any plans that threatened to limit its expansion in New Caledonia.

The Eramet board met on Wednesday to discuss proposals from minority shareholders and to decide the composition of a new board that will be presented for approval at the annual general meeting on July 31.
The new board will include three staff representatives and two people from New Caledonia, who will be named soon.
"They will help us better understand issues in New Caledonia," the spokesman said.
Eramet chairman Yves Rambaud, whose position came under threat during the dispute with the state, is now widely expected to keep his post.
Sources close to the issue said the new board was now fairly balanced between company and state officials, employees and independent members.
"All conditions are there for finding a balanced solution," one source said.
The state wants to give itself more time to review the issue but has already shown it would adopt a less confrontational stance than its predecessor, the sources said.
"We are entering a whole new logic. The method has changed " one source said. Eramet closed up 1.75 percent to 290 francs.
Eramet plans to produce over 60,000 tonnes of nickel in New Caledonia by 2000 from a current level of 54,000 tonnes.
